tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (slow storage, alarms firing, production-readiness, wanting more IOPS) rather than implementation details, explicitly lists numerous trigger contexts including specific CloudWatch metric names and scenarios where the user doesn't mention EBS by name, and ends with explicit exclusions. It is a dense but single, well-structured paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user wants to know why Amazon EBS storage is slow, why an EBS alarm fired, or whether their EBS setup is production-ready, even if they only say an app or database on EC2 got slower or ask whether to add IOPS.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is tightly written, uses tables and bullet lists rather than prose, and focuses on domain-specific classification rules, binding layers, and verdict formats rather than explaining general concepts the agent already knows.
tests.evidence: Load only the reference files the request needs.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The classification table and workflow sections only contain short pointers and link out to references for all detailed material (metric thresholds, API lists, finding logic); no large reference blocks or embedded lookup tables are inlined.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ (data-collection.md, ebs-best-practices.md, finding-logic.md, metrics-thresholds.md, review-operational.md, review-report-format.md, troubleshoot-billing.md, troubleshoot-encryption.md, troubleshoot-performance.md, troubleshoot-snapshots.md, troubleshoot-volume-modification.md) has a markdown link in the body, both in the classification table and in the References section at the bottom.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific trigger condition (user phrasing, alarm type, or workflow step) describing when to load it, rather than a generic 'for details' pointer.
tests.evidence: "My app is slow", high latency, an alarm on AWS/EBS metrics... | Troubleshoot: performance | [references/troubleshoot-performance.md](references/troubleshoot-performance.md)

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All references use the relative 'references/filename.md' format from the skill root with no absolute paths or parent traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical actions (approval requirements, modification limits, binding layer checks) are stated as strict rules, while flexible areas (which path to follow, how to draft findings) allow judgement; the mix is well calibrated to each section's fragility.
tests.evidence: Approval is given only on the approval card. A typed "approve" in chat is not approval.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill does not present multiple competing tools/approaches as equal options; it routes to a single determined path per request type via the classification table rather than offering alternatives to choose from.
tests.evidence: Classification table rows each map to exactly one path/reference, e.g. 'Troubleshoot: performance | [references/troubleshoot-performance.md]'

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable classify-load-run-check approach applicable to any EBS troubleshooting or review request, not a one-off declaration for a specific resource.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Classify the request / Step 2: Load the shared references / Step 3: Run the path and draft the report / Step 4: Check the draft, fix it, then present it

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The Critical Rules section lists concrete, non-obvious domain corrections (e.g., modification limits, CloudTrail optionality, never recommend more provisioning for impairment) that function as gotchas for this storage domain.
tests.evidence: Use current service rules: up to 4 Elastic Volumes modifications per volume per rolling 24 hours... Never recommend more provisioning for an impairment.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill defines both the troubleshoot verdict format and points to a dedicated review-report-format.md reference for the rated report, so structured output templates are addressed appropriately.
tests.evidence: Review mode uses the rated report in [references/review-report-format.md](references/review-report-format.md).

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The inline troubleshoot verdict format is a short 6-item list under 20 lines; the longer rated report format is correctly offloaded to a references file rather than inlined.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 4 is an explicit self-validation pass requiring the agent to check its drafted report against specific criteria (evidence units/time windows, binding layer consistency, recommendation limits, safe-to-delete backing, gaps) before presenting.

Review the draft from Step 3 against these checks. Fix anything that fails, then present it.
